blinding_guess.why: The name /my_topic never appears in the code: rosbridge_server subscribes to whatever a websocket client names, so whether this element works depends on the unseen publisher. Two mechanisms in this snapshot could break delivery for a particular pairing: (1) the first-client subscription copies TRANSIENT_LOCAL / BEST_EFFORT from publishers present at subscribe time only (subscribers.py:117-129), so a publisher that appears later with a BEST_EFFORT profile is never matched; (2) a second client on an already-subscribed topic gets a temporary rclpy subscription created with the integer 10 (depth only, subscribers.py:173-175), and its callback is only promoted into the shared subscriber after that temporary subscription receives a message (subscribers.py:217-233), so with a BEST_EFFORT publisher the second client never receives anything; the multiple_subscribers launch test exists but is not registered in CMakeLists.txt:26-30. Without the pairing I cannot say which, if either, applies; the primary path already carries the publisher-QoS matching and is covered by the best_effort_publisher and transient_local_publisher launch tests.

notes: rosbridge_server 1.1.0 (ROS 2, ament_cmake, Python) is a generic websocket-to-ROS bridge; it declares no topic subscriptions of its own. Consumption of topic:/my_topic happens only at run time: a client sends {"op": "subscribe", "topic": <name>, optional "type", "throttle_rate", "queue_length", "fragment_size", "compression", "id"} (ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:386-419; field list subscribe.py:213-220). Flow: websocket_handler.py:142-147 creates a RosbridgeProtocol per client and an IncomingQueue thread; protocol.py:213-216 dispatches to Subscribe.subscribe (subscribe.py:235-283), which applies the topics_glob allow-list, creates a per-client Subscription (subscribe.py:56-81) and calls SubscriberManager.subscribe (subscribers.py:245-264); the first client on a topic creates a MultiSubscriber that resolves the type (client-supplied or inferred via get_topic_names_and_types; type string compared in pkg/msg/Type form, message_conversion.py:194-200), builds QoSProfile(depth=10, VOLATILE, RELIABLE) then flips durability to TRANSIENT_LOCAL and/or reliability to BEST_EFFORT if any publisher currently on the topic has those (subscribers.py:112-129, comment cites issue #551), and calls node_handle.create_subscription(msg_class, topic, self.callback, qos, raw=raw) (subscribers.py:131-133). Later clients on the same topic go through MultiSubscriber.subscribe (subscribers.py:157-175), which creates a temporary create_subscription(self.msg_class, self.topic, self._new_sub_callback, 10) with no reliability/durability set and migrates the new callbacks on its first message. Messages are wrapped in OutgoingMessage and sent as {"op": "publish", "topic": ..., "msg": ...} with optional png / cbor / cbor-raw encoding (subscribe.py:322-374); throttle_rate (ms) and queue_length are per-client and default to 0 (subscription_modifiers.py). Because no type is fixed, msg_type, frame, units and definition_id are null; the QoS recorded is the base profile written in code, with the conditional override noted in provenance. The element is listed in not_declared because no static declaration or literal reference exists, not because the consumption path is missing; references is empty for the same reason. Provides-side declarations not in the packet: publishers client_count (std_msgs/msg/Int32) and connected_clients (rosbridge_msgs/msg/ConnectedClients), both depth 1 (10 in the script), TRANSIENT_LOCAL (client_mananger.py:44-56; rosbridge_websocket.py:119-127), and parameters retry_startup_delay, use_compression, fragment_timeout, delay_between_messages, max_message_size, unregister_timeout, bson_only_mode, websocket_ping_interval, websocket_ping_timeout, certfile, keyfile, authenticate, port, address, topics_glob, services_glob, params_glob, actual_port (rosbridge_websocket.py:73-134, 299). ros_distro foxy: no dependency definition files were needed or fetched. All 150 snapshot files were listed; the search covered the whole tree, not only rosbridge_server/.
